[h1] Remnant 2 [/h1]

[h2] First Impressions [/h2]
If you're a [i]Destiny[/i] player on the path to recovery but still craving the thrill of shooting things while yelling at your screen, then Remnant 2 is your next fix. It’s like [i]Destiny[/i], but with a side of Souls-like difficulty, which is to say: it will destroy you, but you’ll love every second of it. Also, there’s a dog, and you can pet it—so really, who needs any other reason to play?

[h2] Pros [/h2]

[b]Gunplay that’s crisp, addictive, and oh-so-satisfying.[/b] You’ll be dodging and shooting like John Wick—if John Wick fought giant world bosses and sometimes summoned monsters to do his bidding.
[b]Build diversity is off the charts.[/b] Want to be a sharpshooter with a love for sniping heads? Done. Want to summon minions and let them do all the dirty work while you sip coffee in the corner? Also done.
[b]Procedurally generated maps[/b] keep things fresh. Every playthrough is a new chance to get lost, scream “WHERE AM I?” and then feel like a god when you finally figure it out.
[b]No battle pass, no microtransactions.[/b] Just a game that gives you everything upfront and throws in DLC because it knows you're already hooked.
[b]Co-op mode?[/b] Yes, please. Nothing says “bonding” like screaming “revive me!” at your friends while you dodge the boss’s laser beams.
[b]Doggo.[/b] Did we mention the dog? You can pet it. It’s important.
[h2] Grain of Salt [/h2]

The game doesn’t exactly [i]hold your hand[/i] when it comes to understanding the mechanics. Stats? Scaling? What counts as damage? Good luck figuring that out without a side degree in game design.
Character customization is... let’s call it [i]minimalistic.[/i] Six faces, six voices, a few scars, and hair options. But hey, once you slap some armor on, who’s even looking at your character’s face anymore, right?
You’re going to need some [b]third-party resources[/b] (ahem, a wiki) if you want to unlock everything. There are puzzles and hidden items that you could stumble across—if you’re extraordinarily lucky or have psychic powers. Or, you know, just Google it. We’ve all done it.
[h2] Negatives [/h2]

[b]Balance?[/b] Yeah, about that. Not all archetypes are created equal. Sure, you [i]could[/i] use any combination of classes and weapons, but some choices are like bringing a butter knife to a gunfight. Yes, you’ll survive... eventually. Maybe.
The grind for specific items can be real, especially after your first playthrough. But don’t worry, there’s a world analyzer to help—because no one likes the idea of replaying for 10 hours just to get that one gun.
[b]Story? What story?[/b] It’s there, somewhere, but let’s not pretend you’re playing Remnant 2 for the plot. You’re here to blow stuff up, and the game knows it.
[h2] The Verdict: 7.3/10 [/h2]
If you’re in the market for a game that’s like Dark Souls but with guns, and you’re okay with occasionally using a wiki to figure out how to unlock something obscure (looking at you, Archon), then Remnant 2 is for you. It’s tough, it’s fast-paced, and it’ll keep you coming back for more, especially with its build diversity and challenging boss fights. Plus, the co-op mode is fantastic for adding a social element to your suffering.

In short, grab the game, try all the ridiculous builds, pet the dog, and prepare to have fun—and possibly throw your controller a few times.
Bad optimization and overall worse game compared to the first one.

Runs badly due to gunfire using frame-generation on unreal engine 5 to make up for their lack of willingness to just optimize the game and make it run well. I love the QoL the game offered but I'd rather play the first game due to how poor this one runs.

Pros:
-Gunplay is great 
-Enemies and Environments are super cool
-Co-op is really fun
-Price is decent
-Ability to use 2 classes at once is cool and allows fun combinations
-The new miniboss elite thing they do can be really cool

Cons:
-Melee sucks
-The dodge is atrocious imo
-The story is boring
-Trait point caps and nerfed gear try to enforce the use of builds, I personally hate feeling like I'm forced to use a build
-Traits are now only acquired via Tomes and defeating the bosses, meaning no more getting trait points via leveling up
-Almost every enemy aside from the most basic cannon fodder (and even then, some of those) feel like unnecessary bullet sponges, even with high level gear, making them all really annoying to kill, especially when you're stuck fighting hoards of them
-You will get attacked by elites every five steps
-the new miniboss elite thing they do can be REALLY annoying
-The prism system seems unnecessarily complicated and the exp requirements for leveling them adds an awful exp grind to the game
-The prism shards adds yet another awful grind to the prism system (two if you count finding the shards themselves and the relic dust as separate grinds)

I REALLY REALLY want to like this game, I absolutely loved Remnant 1 and was the probably biggest hype man for this game in my friend group when it was announced, I even pre-ordered the Ult. edition, because of which, i'm going to continue to sink hours into this, seeing as how its been over a year and I only just now beat the main story. Unfortunately, I can't recommend this to anyone. It feels like they just took the first game and made it grindier, harder, and more complicated just for the sake of being that way. Any new mechanics feel like they were added just to fluff playtime, There's a reason Remnant 2 lost %80 of it's playerbase after the first month. Just play the first one, you'll have a better time.

EDIT: These are my personal Praises/Gripes with the game and only reflect my opinion. Others may enjoy what I don't, regardless, if you do buy the game it will probably still be several hours of fun.

Gameplay 8/10 Very solid, they made dark souls with guns work, had so much fun
Story 1/10 The story is so bad that infact i`d rather be on a israeli fishing vessel in the red sea about to be stricked by a houthi missile launched from a tent in the dessert then not skip a cutscene expetialy if the asian dog named clementine is in it ( we spent a total of 5 min with this dog in the game, and we go on a whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mission to find her )
can't recommend the game enough, "Praise the Gun"
